NSAID-induced liver injury (NSAID-IDILI) is a common and serious adverse event.
NSAID-induced liver injury (NSAID-ILI) is associated with synergism between NSAIDs and cytokines that is mediated by caspases and mitogen- activated protein kinases ( MAPKs).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of drug/cytokines interactions in the pathogenesis of IDILI.
a new mechanism of drug toxicity, namely, the synergistic interaction between a drug and cytokines to cause cell death.
a novel mechanism of drug-induced liver injury, namely, drug/cytokines synergy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanism by which NSAID/cytotoxicity synergizes is not known, but it is likely that the mechanism is complex and that different NSAIDs have different mechanisms.
NSAIDs that are AA derivatives and cause IDILIs are synergized by cytokines to cause cytotoxicity in hepatocytes through caspases and ERK and JNK.
NSAIDs that are AA derivatives and associated with idiosyncratically caused hepatotoxicity synergize with TNFα and IFNγ in causing cytotoxic effects in HepG2 cell lines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NSAID/cytokinetic interactions are a mechanism for idiosyncrasy, and the MAPKs are a key component in this mechanism.
NSAIDs that are AA derivatives are more prone to synergize with cytokines in causing IDILI than NSAIDs that are PA derivatives, and this synergy is driven by JNK and ERK.
cytokines and NSAIDs interact to kill hepatocytes, and this interaction is mediated by caspases and mitogen- activated protein kinases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NSAID/cytokinemediated cytotoxicity involves caspase and MAPK pathways.
NSAIDs that cause idiosyncrasy in animal models and humans interact with cytokines in vitro in a manner that is consistent with a pathogenic mechanism for idiosyncracy.

the MAPKs ERK, JNK, and p38 are involved in the cytotoxic synergy between TNFα and NSAIDs that is associated with idiosyncratically induced liver injury, and the ERK pathway is involved in the cytolytic synergy of NSAIDs with IFNγ.
